rules_evaluated.evidence: Strategy doc M2 mood: 'grounded competence — I can feel when a plan is good before approving it, and I know the move is two reads, not one.' The file frames exactly that and does not resolve it. Big Idea L6: 'The first plan is plausible. Plausible isn't good enough, and you are the one who can tell the difference.' — discernment-you-own, i.e. grounded competence, and L28 states the two-reads move ('Two reads on one plan catch different misses'). Line closest to violating: L84 'Come without one and you'll be picking while the walk is already underway. Your call.' — a stakes beat inside a mechanical M3-task-selection step (§1's setup-beat exemption: this is get-into-position, not a teaching beat), and it ends on 'Your call', which keeps agency with the student rather than flattening competence into compliance. State the exit mood in one sentence: the student leaves able to read a plan and holding a self-chosen M3 task, with the leverage horizon (L50's second loop, the inlined 'where the rule could live' closer at L38) opened and deliberately unresolved — which is what M3's earned-trust beat needs to still have work to do.

M2's mood is grounded competence, not unease, so the trigger condition is weak here — but one line invites a recalled failure and is worth scoring rather than waving off. L26: 'when was the last time you entered generation with too little planning? Where did it bite: wrong files, a design decided mid-run, rework you could have planned away?' The register is diagnostic, not confessional: the three named outcomes are conditions of the run (wrong files / a mid-run design call / rework), never traits of the student, and there is no 'you should have' anywhere in the body. Flavour is 'I did not yet know what to look for', which is the not-knowing side of the split, not the having-done-wrong side.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Lead with discipline, not failure mode.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Title (L1) 'Plan mode, done right' and Big Idea (L6) both name a positive discipline — discernment before approval — not a failure word. Line closest to violating: L21 '- **Spot** approval inflation in a plan whose structure makes it look decided' — 'approval inflation' is a failure mode, but it sits as the OBJECT of a discipline verb ('Spot'), which is precisely the shape §3 prescribes ('failure mode becomes the negative case the discipline addresses, not the title'). Key Concepts opens on the discipline too (L45 'Structure is persuasive…'), not on the failure. No Big Idea, WYL bullet or Key Concept is failure-titled, so the named-canonical-result carve-out is not needed.

Four sequencing claims pulled from § 'M2 in detail' and checked mechanically against the body projection (curriculum/evals/body-views/ae101--module--plan-mode-done-right.body.txt, 85 lines). (a) 'M2 doesn't front-run M3's first-Skill-use moment' + 'M3 still owns first skill invocation and authoring': grep -niE '\b(skill|subagent|hook|hooks|eval|evals|worktree|MCP)\b' → 2 hits, both L46 and L49, and both are the craft sense ('where the plan-reading skill lives', 'The skill is old; only the surface is new'), not the Skill primitive; grep validated against a planted 'Remember: (Analyze) skill subagent' string → 1. (b) 'Approve. Stop. No execution… running the code is M3's concern': L49 'You don't have to execute a plan to know it's good' states the refusal rather than breaching it; no bullet asks the student to run anything. (c) 'M2 issues no homework' — no `## Homework` heading; maintainer note L104 records the call. (d) The `## Next` block (L78) hands M3 its task without teaching M3's access-surface material, and the M3 pre-reads (L62–70) are flagged as optional reading, not taught. Line closest to violating: L14's Horthy callback, which names the cure ('human review made affordable by upfront planning') — that is M2's own subject, not a downstream module's.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Strategic themes recur in Key Concepts.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Walking the six `## Key Concepts` bullets (L45–L50) and naming the theme each instances: L45 'Assume about 10% of it is wrong and go find which part' → theme 1 (Claude is 90% correct), in M2's own plan-reading language; L50 'A rule that doesn't load doesn't exist, and where you put it decides when it fires. Fixing the plan is the first loop; changing the rule that shaped it is the second' → theme 2 (compounding builds the system) and theme 5 (capture your world — the loading-model choice is the concrete capture beat the strategy doc names for the second exercise); L46 'A human read and an agent's walk-down catch different misses. The gap between them is where the plan-reading skill lives' → theme 3 (the LLM is a mirror; the operator's read is half the instrument). That is ≥3 theme-instances, each phrased in the module's own register with no theme named aloud. Line closest to violating: L48 ('A plan with a specific file list has made decisions…') is the most purely tactical bullet with no theme behind it — it survives because §5 requires 2–3 theme-instances per section, not per bullet.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Key Concepts shape — theme breadcrumbs, not standalone section.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Gates first: every bullet L45–L50 is emergent (each names something the two exercises produce, none lectures a move before doing it), none is failure-led (§3 above), none front-runs M3 (§4 grep above). Breadcrumb count is inside the 1–3 range: L45 closes on 'Assume about 10% of it is wrong and go find which part' — directional, names the move rather than a trust ratio, exactly the §6 hazard the rule flags — and L49 closes on 'The skill is old; only the surface is new.' Scored by reading, not by marker: grep -nE 'Remember:' → 0 and no bolded breadcrumb wrapper exists, consistent with the retired-form note the rule warns judges not to re-file. Adjacency check per the variety clause: M1 `getting-going.md` Key Concepts close on 'Context is what you put in it.' and 'One ticket is enough to start reading them back'; M3 `earn-the-trust.md` on 'Invoke, don't re-derive.' and 'an untested skill in the team kit is slop-sharing' — no verbatim or near-verbatim repeat with M2's two, and different themes fire. Maintainer note L106 already accepts the 10% line's register and hedge; not re-raised. No 'Themes this module instances:' section exists.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: What You'll Learn shape — capability register, not syllabus.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Gates first: no bullet is failure-led (§3) and none front-runs M3 (§4 grep). Apparatus check is mechanical and clean — grep -nE '\((Analyze|Evaluate|Create|Understand|Apply)\)' over the body → 0 hits (validated against a planted '(Analyze)' string → 1), so no Bloom parentheticals; no 'not a…' author-defence aside appears in L18–L22; no definition-stamping triplet colon. Register test on each bullet stripped to verb + immediate object: run plan mode / push back twice / walk down branches / spot approval inflation / extract task-shaping rules — all five read as work another engineer would recognise, none as something the curriculum does to the student. Line closest to violating: L19 '- **Push back** twice on the plan via *No, keep planning*, surfacing what the agent didn't see' — the participial tail is the nearest thing to a §7(ii) mechanism tail, but it names the OUTCOME of the move, not the pedagogical apparatus that produces it ('by mapping…', 'by walking…'), and the verb+object still leads. L22's trailing 'into a `.md` file you place' is carve-out (a): the artifact the student walks away with, destination after the practice, not object-leads-with-destination.
